# Which memory, when, at what cost

> **Provider note.** Conversations and judge calls ran 12 at a time, not one after another. Recall, tokens and cost are unaffected. Latency was measured under the benchmark's own load and is not comparable with a one-at-a-time run; for memory read and write latency use scripts/memory_latency.py.

Source: [`aggregate.json`](../results/runs/20261116T155056861215Z-v2/aggregate.json) and [`manifest.json`](../results/runs/20261116T155056861215Z-v2/manifest.json) of run `20261116T155056861215Z-v2`. 3 runs of 30 turns, checkpoints 10, 20, 30, answering model `anthropic-claude-sonnet-5.5`, judge `openai-gpt-6-sol`, embeddings `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, k = 4. Cost is recorded tokens at $2.00 per million input tokens and $10.00 per million output tokens (`anthropic-claude-sonnet-5.5`, source: https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/gradient-ai-platform/details/pricing/, checked 2026-11-16). List price, no prompt caching discount.

How to read the figures:

- **Recall** is the mean of per-run recall with a 95% Student t interval over runs. It leaves out the `abstention` and `sensitive` categories, which are shown on their own under recall by category. With few runs the interval is wide. Two backends whose intervals overlap are not separated by this run; that is not the same as being equal.
- **Cost per conversation** covers the answering calls and memory upkeep (summary rewrites, fact extraction). **Cost per correct recall** is conversation spend plus headline probe spend, divided by the headline probes answered correctly.
- **Memory latency** is the time the memory itself adds to a turn: the read before the answer and the write after it. For `summary` and `mem0` the write includes an LLM call.

## Pick this when

Each line is produced by a fixed rule in `src/site/guide.py` from the tables that follow. The rules compare 95% intervals, so they say "not separated" far more often than "better".

- **Highest recall:** `buffer`, `summary`, `mem0` at 100.0% [91, 100].
- **This run does not separate any backend from the best on recall:** every interval overlaps the best one's. On this evidence the choice comes down to cost and latency; more runs would be needed to rank recall.
- **Pick `pgvector` when you want the cheapest backend whose recall is not separated from the best:** $0.1935 per conversation at 94.7% [83, 100] recall. The highest-recall backend, `buffer`, costs $0.3906 per conversation, 2.0 times as much.
- **Pick `pgvector` when the unit you pay for is a correct answer:** $0.0211 per correct recall, the lowest of all backends, at 94.7% [83, 100] recall.
- **Pick `buffer` when the memory must add the least time to a turn** (among the backends not separated from the best): 0.0 ms read plus 0.0 ms write at p50. Compare that with the answering call's p50 of 3,899 ms before treating it as a reason.
- **For single facts stated once** (`extraction`): every backend scored 100%, so this category does not tell them apart (up to 18 probes each).
- **For facts that are corrected later** (`update`): `buffer`, `summary`, `mem0` scored highest, 100% (up to 10 probes each; see the table for the intervals, which are wide).
- **For date arithmetic across turns** (`temporal`): every backend scored 100%, so this category does not tell them apart (up to 5 probes each).
- **For combining two facts from different turns** (`multi_hop`): every backend scored 100%, so this category does not tell them apart (up to 4 probes each).
- **For saying so when the user never told it (highest rate means it makes things up least)** (`abstention`): 5 backends tied (all except `mem0`) and scored highest, 100% (up to 18 probes each; see the table for the intervals, which are wide).

## What this guide does not cover

It reports one run configuration: one answering model, one embedding model, synthetic conversations of the length given above, and a single user. The design record ([DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md), sections 6 and 7) lists what that leaves open.
